title: NI record framing
rule: An NI record is its payload prefixed with the payload length as four big-endian bytes. The prefix is peer-controlled and must be bounded before it is allocated against.
provenance: Authored in open-rfc-go from the behaviour of open-rfc src/protocol/ni.ts and test/ni.test.ts at commit 847036d. See conformance/README.md for the intended move upstream.

encode.name: three-byte payload
encode.why: The canonical case, byte-identical to upstream test/ni.test.ts.

encode.name: empty payload
encode.why: A zero-length record is a bare length prefix, not an error.

encode.name: payload containing a length-prefix lookalike
encode.why: Framing is length-driven, never content-driven: payload bytes that look like a header must not resynchronise the decoder.

decode.name: two records in one chunk
decode.why: Coalesced records must both be delivered from a single read.

decode.name: one record split across every byte boundary
decode.why: The length prefix itself may straddle reads; a decoder that assumes four contiguous bytes fails on a slow link.

decode.name: record split mid-payload
decode.why: Reads have no relationship to record boundaries.

decode.name: advertised length above the configured limit
decode.why: The bound is checked against the advertised length before any allocation, so a hostile prefix cannot force one.

decode.name: advertised length exactly at the configured limit
decode.why: The bound is inclusive. Rejecting the boundary value is the classic off-by-one that refuses valid traffic.

decode.name: stream ends mid-payload
decode.why: A peer that closes mid-record must be reported, not silently treated as a clean end of stream. The prefix stays buffered with the partial payload: an incomplete record is retained whole, never partially delivered.

decode.name: stream ends mid-prefix
decode.why: Two buffered bytes are not yet a length; the decoder must retain rather than guess.
